Since the last green dev run on 20 Oct, two gates have broken without any code change. Every new PR to dev or main goes red (#589, #590), and Deploy dev cannot build its image.

## Changes

- **Dependency audit.** `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` fails on GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5: zod 3.25.76, nested under `expo/@expo/cli`.
  - The only fix is zod 4.6.6. Even the latest `@expo/cli` still declares `^3.25.76`.
  - This PR adds a scoped override: `"@expo/cli": { "zod": "4.6.6" }`.
  - `@expo/cli` uses zod only in two dev-server DevTools schema files. Their calls (`object`, `enum`, `union`, `literal`, `string().url()`, `readonly`, `safeParse`, `error.issues`) all exist in zod 4, and both schemas parse correctly under 4.6.6.
- **Runtime image.** `deploy/Dockerfile` pinned `ffmpeg=8.1.2-r0`, which Alpine 3.24 no longer ships; `apk policy ffmpeg` in the pinned base image lists only `8.1.3-r0`. That broke Release security run 40140169755 and would break Deploy dev at the bundle build. The pin is now `8.1.3-r0`.

## Checks

- `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`: 0 vulnerabilities.
- `npm run build:web`: exported.
- `npm run test:fast`: all suites pass (root, server 985 passed / 21 skipped, frontend 1674).
- Release security, triggered by the path filter, builds and scans both images in CI.
title: fix(ci): unblock the dependency audit and runtime image build

body:
Overnight follow-up cleanup after #581. One branch, one PR. Behaviour changes were pinned by tests first, and each commit message names what it deletes.

## What and why

**1. SQLite migration squash (owner-authorised)**
- Migrations 1–31 are squashed into `server/migrations/sqlite-baseline.sql`, which is the exact `sqlite_master` SQL the old chain produced for a fresh database.
- `MIGRATIONS` in `server/src/schema.ts` now lists only the receipts: `{ version, key }` for versions 1–31.
- A fresh SQLite database runs the baseline once and records every version and key. Its receipts are therefore the same as those of databases built by the old chain, and the same as PostgreSQL's. `deploy/release.py` still reads `schema_version` 31 from `schema.ts`.
- A database already at version 31 opens with no change.
- A database that is older, partly migrated, or has lost receipts is refused. The error says to upgrade it first with a release from before the squash, tagged **`pre-migration-squash`** (pushed, pointing at d38a559).
- Readiness now also reports a dropped baseline table, index or trigger as `baseline:<name>`.
- About 1,300 lines of per-migration repair code are gone, along with the 31 SQL files and the ledger schema repair helpers.
- **Equivalence proof.** `server/tests/migration-baseline.test.mjs` uses `fixtures/sqlite-schema-v31.json`. That fixture was generated once from the old chain at d38a559 and covers, for every table: normalised `sqlite_master` SQL, `table_xinfo`, `foreign_key_list`, `index_list` with `index_xinfo`, and row contents. The test checks four things:
  - the baseline produces exactly that schema;
  - a version-31 database is untouched (schema cookie, receipts and snapshot all unchanged);
  - a version-29 database is refused;
  - a database that has tables but no receipts is refused, not overwritten.
- **PostgreSQL is not squashed.** It is already one baseline (030) plus a single six-line 031. Merging them would save nothing, and could strand a database prepared at version 30, such as release PostgreSQL ahead of #562's cutover. Hosted dev PostgreSQL at 31 is a no-op either way.
- **Tests removed** because they only exercised retired legacy upgrade or repair paths. Each is named in the commit.
- **Assertions changed from "repair" to "report and refuse"**, as listed in the commit.

**2. Audit actor**
- `recordAuditEvent` used to keep only `demo-` synthetic actors, so every real action recorded a null actor.
- It now records the signed-in member's profile id. The column stays a foreign key to profiles, and real accounts are mirrored there one-to-one, so the account is reachable via `real_profiles.account_id`.
- System and scheduler actions, and unknown ids, record null.
- Tests: `real-archive` pinned the null actor first, then the assertion was intentionally updated. New `audit.test.mjs`.

**3. Leftovers**
- `docs/design/playback.md` now says bytes are served only via `/media/access/:token`. Stale migration links in the docs were repointed.
- The service worker no longer special-cases the removed `/films/` and `/clips/` prefixes. `/media/` and `/api/` stay uncached, and `pwa.test.mjs` still covers `/clips/...`.
- The `make run-real` dev proxy now destroys the upstream request when the client disconnects, as `production-web-proxy` already does. This stops leaked SSE streams and the resulting 429s.
- The false "session expired or an administrator reset your password" message: the cause was a stale session cookie that was never cleared, so every later visit reported it. `/auth/session` now clears the cookie with its `session_expired` 401. The message therefore shows once, when a real session was lost, and later visits are plain signed-out visits. The test pinned the old behaviour first.
- "First cycle lasts four weeks" copy is **left as is**: the client cannot know `REWIND_REAL_CYCLE_MINUTES` before a group exists.
- The new explainer site (`docs/site`) is updated for all of the above, and its html is regenerated.

**4. Power controller removed and applied**
- Nothing started or stopped the dev host: state had no automatic-start schedule, no workflow invoked the Lambda, and the host runs 24/7 since #519.
- Removed `demo/automation.tf`, `lambda/power_controller.py`, the `automatic_start_*` variables and the wake-guard allowances.
- **Terraform** (`AWS_PROFILE=rewind-terraform-apply`):
  - The full plan showed the nine power-controller destroys plus one **pre-existing** drift: `aws_lightsail_instance_public_ports.rewind[0]` must be replaced. That drift is also present on the unchanged code, because the SSH rule was changed to `lightsail-connect` outside Terraform.
  - To leave the host firewall alone, I applied a **targeted** plan of exactly the nine addresses: `Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 9 to destroy` → `Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 0 changed, 9 destroyed.`
  - Destroyed: the Lambda, its log group, IAM role and policy, the `rewind-demo-operator` and `rewind-demo-scheduler` roles and policies, and the `rewind-demo` schedule group.
  - The host is still `running`. A re-plan shows only the pre-existing ports drift.

**5. Simplification**
- One `beginImmediate` / `isBusyError` helper (`server/src/sqlite-busy.ts`) replaces five copies of the busy-retry loop.
- `server/src/jobs/index.ts` (2,121 lines) is split into `compilation`, `clip`, `stored-output`, `staged-cleanup`, `audited` and `shared`. `media/index.ts` (1,321 lines) is split into `staged-source`, `clip-upload` and `clip-policy`. Both splits are pure moves, and each `index.ts` remains a re-export barrel.
- Dead exports removed: `transitionCycleLifecycle` and `processCycleLifecycle` aliases, `src/domain/cycles.ts`, `CaptureCapabilityError` and `CapturePermissionError`, a duplicate `PHOTO_SECONDS`, a re-export, and `ChatHistoryPage`. Several internals were un-exported.
- Flake fixed: `http-route-contract-auth.test.mjs` built its Cognito fixture with a top-level await *after* registering tests. The runner closed the first runtime mid-login ("database is not open"), and the Cognito test never ran. The file now runs 86/86.

## Verification
- `npm run test:fast`: root, server and frontend all passed (frontend 1674 tests).
- `npm run test:slow`: 41 responsive tests plus two real-account HTTPS runs passed.
- `npm run test:a11y`: 6/6.
- `typecheck`, `lint`, `architecture:check` and `format:check` are clean.
- `make test-postgres` passes (0 fail).
- Deploy fixtures (`wake-recovery-selection`, `recovery-smoke`) pass.
- `make run-real` smoke via the proxy on :8090 passed every step:
  - a fresh visit returns `session_required`;
  - register, sign in, create group, upload and process a photo, send a chat message and read history;
  - 8 SSE connect/abort cycles, all 200 (the limit is 5);
  - a stale cookie gets `session_expired` once and the cookie is cleared, and the next visit returns `session_required`.

## LOC (non-doc lines, origin/dev → this branch)
| area | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| src (+App.tsx) | 24,906 | 24,854 |
| server/src | 24,729 | 23,531 |
| server/migrations | 1,333 | 1,157 |
| tests (tests + server/tests) | 66,883 | 66,380 |
| infra | 3,484 | 3,131 |

The schema snapshot fixture (`.json`) is excluded from these counts.

## Follow-ups
- `infra/terraform/bootstrap/access.tf` still lists the now-deleted `rewind-demo-operator` role in the operator's assume-role policy. This is harmless and needs a bootstrap apply. The `rewind-demo-operator` profile in `~/.aws/config` can also go.
- Reconcile the dev host SSH ports drift in Terraform: either adopt `lightsail-connect` in `lightsail.tf` or re-apply.
- After the next full demo apply, the `archive` provider can be dropped from `demo/versions.tf`; it is kept only for stale data sources still in state.
- Release cutover (#562) must import any SQLite snapshot older than 31 with `main` as it is now, or with tag `pre-migration-squash`, not with a post-squash build.

Higher-risk follow-up to the 20 Oct cleanup (#578). **Please review before merging.** It touches private media routes and Terraform, which AGENTS.md leaves to the owner.

Method: characterisation tests were written and committed first, run green against the old code, and kept green through every refactor commit.

## Tests added first
- Server HTTP route contract: `server/tests/http-route-contract-{auth,media,real}.test.mjs`, plus shared `helpers/runtime.mjs` and `helpers/route-contract.mjs`.
- Media access denials on `/media/access` (cross-group, other member, tampered media, sealed archive), ported before the legacy routes were removed.
- Client screens: `tests/{camera-capture,video-capture,settings,report-sheet,group-experience,group-experience-capture}.characterisation.test.tsx`.

## Changes
- **Removed legacy direct media routes:** `GET/HEAD /films/:id/play`, `/films/:id/download`, `/clips/:id/download`, `GET /films/:id`, `/downloads/:id`, and their db helpers. The client only uses `/media/access`. `GET /clips/:id` (upload status) stays.
- **`server/src/http.ts`, 4k → 235 lines:** split into route-table modules under `server/src/routes/`, with shared `respond`, `body`, `context` and `limits` helpers.
- **`db.ts`, about 2.1k → 776 lines:** SQLite migrations and repair steps moved unchanged to `schema.ts`. **No migration was removed**, because release still runs SQLite.
- **Large screens split:**
  - `VideoCaptureScreen` (about 2k → 285 lines) into hooks and panels.
  - `Settings.tsx` (1.4k → 38 lines) into step components, with a shared `RadioList` also used by `ReportSheet`.
  - `RealAccountGroupExperience` (1.3k → 559 lines) into `use-group-membership-flows` and `GroupNotices`.
- **Removed Demo capture leftovers:** `DemoCameraPlatform`, the `kind === 'demo'` branches, the `demo-fixture` sources, the local-only save path, and the unused `revealState` / `onOpenArchive` / `onAccepted` / system-camera props. This also deletes `src/domain/reveal-education.ts`. The test double moved to `tests/mocks/`.
- **Removed the unapplied second media Terraform path:** `infra/terraform/environments/`, `modules/private-media`, `modules/environment-identity`, `bootstrap/environment-identity.tf`, the `terraform-environments.yml` workflow and its scripts and tests. The state bucket has no `rewind/dev` or `rewind/prod` state, and a read-only bootstrap plan showed no infrastructure change, so no apply is needed. The live roots (bootstrap, demo, media, release) are untouched.
- **Consolidations:**
  - Shared server test runtime/database helpers.
  - Shared JSON POST client request and a JSON `Response` test stub.
  - Local media directories named once.
  - One deploy-fixture runner (`tests/deploy/run-fixtures.sh`) replaces three copies of the list.
  - `scaffold.test.mjs` no longer re-runs other tests.
  - Removed the deploy README prose pins and the test-only `setStagedSourcePath`.
- **Bug fix found by the new tests:** "Try again" after a failed photo capture did nothing. The new test fails before the fix.
- Design-doc source anchors updated to point at the moved code.

## Not done
- **Power-controller Lambda:** removing it needs a Terraform apply on the dev host, so it was left alone.
- **Audit actor semantics:** a product decision.
- **Squashing SQLite migrations:** unsafe until the release PostgreSQL cutover.

## Size
Non-doc lines by area, `dev` → branch:

| Area | `dev` | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| `src` | 22.9k | 23.9k |
| `server/src` | 24.8k | 24.7k |
| `tests` + `server/tests` | 61.0k | 66.9k |
| `infra` | 5.1k | 3.5k |

This is mostly restructuring for readability rather than a cut in line count: the large files were split into focused modules, and about 5.9k lines of behavioural tests were added.

## Verification (local, after merging the latest `dev`)
- `npm run test:fast`: root, server, and 1,674 frontend tests pass.
- `npm run test:slow` passes. `npm run test:a11y`: 6 passed.
- `make test-postgres`: 988 passed, 0 failed.
- Frontend coverage: 89.6% statements, 92.3% lines (was 87% / 90%). Server coverage: about 86% lines, 85.7% branches.
- Typecheck, lint and architecture checks are clean.
- Manual smoke on `make run`: account creation → group creation (RadioList) → photo capture from file → Seal (upload 201, process 200) → chat send/receive.

Android photo capture reached review but Seal failed with HTTP 400 `upload_intent_invalid_media` at completion. Expo Camera 57.0.6’s native Android result returns `.jpg` / `.png`, despite the `jpg` / `png` TypeScript declaration. Forwarding `.jpg` made the photo session declare valid JPEG bytes as `image/png`.

Normalize canonical and dotted JPEG/PNG values at the camera adapter boundary and reject unknown/missing formats. Preserve file bytes, dimensions, hash, idempotency, group checks, allowance, and existing transfer/server validation. Increment the internal APK to versionCode 4 to distinguish it from installed code 3; no public distribution is performed.

Refs #574.

Validation: the original owned photo is pinned to one exact version; idempotent completion returns 400 `upload_intent_invalid_media`, while its checkpoint declares image/png. Fresh owned native capture is an actual 1080×2400 JPEG (21,167 bytes), saved under a doubled-dot suffix by the old adapter. Regression tests fail before the fix; all 54 focused tests and test:fast pass after it (660 frontend tests). Normal commit/push hooks pass unchanged.

A fresh versionCode 4 APK built successfully from `1b70716c05b6808e0eff9cb44446619a7658bdb0` through the existing offline Gradle route with Java 17. Package `com.anonymous.rewindapp`, unchanged signer SHA-256 `fac61745dc0903786fb9ede62a962b399f7348f0bb6f899b8332667591033b9c`. The source receipt verifies the application sources and embedded bundle. APK SHA-256 `bd618636e0dbd3aa854648860df449dbb2cf603608c02c7b8cc5a19fb95fdbef` (105,690,049 bytes), retained locally as an unmerged internal preview; no public release or distribution performed.

On Android 16/API 36 emulator-5554, in-place upgrade preserved the owned Developer session/group and firstInstallTime. A new native JPEG (1080×2400, 21,397 bytes) sealed with one tap. Its declared image/jpeg, byte length, and SHA-256 exactly match the captured bytes; the read-only owned intent lookup returns HTTP 200, completed, with a contribution. After a cold restart, Your moments explicitly lists “Photo · 3 s · Today · sealed” alongside the prior sealed 15-second video, and Home shows 2 of 5 / 18 of 30 seconds. The previous failed transfer was not relabeled or re-uploaded. Physical-device/released-film checks are not claimed. Parent owns the independent Sol review and merge.
title: fix: preserve JPEG MIME type for native photo sealing

Android capture was rejected on every emulator because capability depended on `Device.isDevice`. Use Expo Device’s Android PackageManager feature checks for camera and microphone independently, preserving permission checks, fail-closed probe errors, and unsupported iOS simulators. Increment Android versionCode to 3 for the fresh embedded client.

Refs #572.

Validation: capture-platform tests pass (47); test:fast and normal commit/push hooks pass (54 frontend suites, 653 tests, 77.37% statement coverage). The file-system test mock declares ES-module identity so its existing mutable cacheDirectory assertion reaches the adapter; assertions remain intact.

The existing offline preparation/Gradle route built a fresh APK with installed Java 17. Package `com.anonymous.rewindapp`, versionCode 3, same debug signer `fac61745dc0903786fb9ede62a962b399f7348f0bb6f899b8332667591033b9c`. APK SHA-256 `aa85254e61997c5b874f8b4c818090e464f2b788c1d54b407e474be7386e09a8` (105,689,853 bytes). Native source receipt verifies 71 application sources and the embedded bundle against commit `9c60ee762cf10d7988a51b9325af5bf1d18c9673`. Build remains an unmerged internal preview; no release published.

On Android 16/API 36 emulator-5554, in-place upgrade retained firstInstallTime, a fresh owned Developer account, and its owned group. Camera permission, live native preview, and photo capture into review pass. Microphone permission, native video recording to the 15-second cap, and preview playback pass. The generated native MP4 contains H264 1280×720 video with -90° rotation and an AMR audio track, duration 14.9846 seconds. These are simulated-hardware results; audible host-microphone content and physical-device capture are unverified. No media injection or Device/property spoofing was used.

Downstream limitation: photo Seal fails with “The contribution could not be accepted. Check its status and capture allowance.” Video Seal completes asynchronously: after cold restart Home shows 1 of 5 moments / 15 of 30 seconds, and Your moments explicitly lists “Video · 15 s · Today · sealed”. Film/export remain unverified because this owned group has no released film. Account/group creation, cold restart, invite generation, and revocation pass; the UI confirms “Code revoked. Make a new one when you need it.” These do not change the camera/microphone hardware result. Parent owns independent Sol review, merge, and downstream coordination.
title: fix: detect Android camera and microphone hardware

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.2 to 4.39.0
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

Release notes

Sourced from @​aws-sdk/client-cognito-identity-provider's releases.

v3.1152.0

3.1152.0(2026-10-14)

Documentation Changes
  • client-marketplace-metering: Documentation update - added a Get started pointer to the AWS Marketplace AI Metering Agent Skill in the BatchMeterUsage API reference. No API or behavior change. (c97db282)
New Features
  • clients: update client endpoints as of 2026-10-14 (91a8a07c)
  • client-imagebuilder: This release adds parentInstance to infrastructure configurations, so builds can use an already-running instance from an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. It also adds terminateInstanceOnCompletion, which keeps build and test instances running after image creation ends. (e8a5e26b)
  • client-cloudfront: This release adds a new "IpAddressType" field to "VPCOriginEndpointConfig", allowing customers to specify whether their VPC origin accepts IPv4-only or dualstack connections. (6bae6413)
  • client-transfer: AWS Transfer Family now lets you store SFTP server host keys in AWS Secrets Manager in your own AWS account. This gives you greater control over your server identity and helps simplify server migrations and failover. (9d0e8866)
  • client-dynamodb-streams: Add support for a new iterator type (AT TIMESTAMP) for DynamoDB Streams GetShardIterator API that allows reading from a specific point in time from the stream. (150e6ae3)
  • client-ec2: Adds T8i instance sizes to the InstanceType enum. T8i instances are low-cost burstable instances powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon 6 processors, available exclusively on AWS, and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards (65c6056b)
  • client-arc-region-switch: Features - Adds support for an optional payload to invoke the Lambda function with as part of the Custom action Lambda execution block (d21aa72b)
  • client-organizations: With dual-stack enabled, all requests now resolve to the endpoint in the partition's primary Region (for example, organizations.us-east-1.api.aws) and are signed for that Region. Previously, requests from other Regions resolved to a nonexistent endpoint. No API changes. (9324745e)
  • client-bedrock-agentcore-control: This release supports scoping Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway rate limits by request header or request body field. (30c5bca2)
  • client-lambda: AWS Lambda now supports an optional X-Ray trace header for chained invocations in durable executions, enabling child invocations to be linked to the initiating span. (08219be0)
  • client-guardduty: Releasing support for Custom Detection Rule Runtime Monitoring (0cb32b8f)
  • lib-transfer-manager: publish as a preview package (#8355) (41080929)

For list of updated packages, view updated-packages.md in assets-3.1152.0.zip

v3.1151.0

3.1151.0(2026-10-13)

Chores
  • lib-transfer-manager: move lib-transfer-manager to preview/ folder (#8351) (5037a006)
  • scripts: add preview/ folder to build tooling (#8350) (a922905a)
Documentation Changes
  • client-lambda-web: Documentation update to include common use cases. (643507a0)
New Features
  • clients: update client endpoints as of 2026-10-13 (d3994582)
  • client-lakeformation: Added new LakeFormation APIs and documentation updates for Simple Row-level Security (RLS). (c7a586fc)
  • client-agent-registry-control: AWS Agent Registry is improving recently launched custom metadata schema feature to make shared attributes easier to manage. (ed00d0bb)
  • client-omics: With Expanded container registry support, you can use container images from registries such as Seqera (Wave), NVIDIA NGC, and Google Artifact Registry with AWS HealthOmics private workflows, without manually migrating images into Amazon ECR or editing your workflow definitions. (db382740)
  • client-route-53-domains: Route 53 Domains now supports premium domains. This release adds consent objects to operations on premium domains and a new GetDomainPrices API. Also, the Flags and PublicKey fields were deprecated from the DnssecKey response. (c5cc6f50)
  • client-gamelift: Adds support for new instance types in the C8a, C8i, C9g, M8a, M8i, and M9g families for managed EC2 and container fleets (51456772)
  • client-appstream: Adds support for administrators to require users to re-authenticate OneDrive and Google Drive storage connectors when a streaming session is reused. (2b6f2af5)
  • client-connect: New APIs to support aliases and versions for ContactFlow. (39466baa)
  • client-appintegrations: This release adds the Connect JWT authentication type and the AudienceOverride field to AuthConfig, letting A2A server applications authenticate with JWTs issued by Amazon Connect. (3b212b20)

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.63.0 to 1.64.1
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.64.1

Bug Fixes

  • #43247 [Bug]: _electron.launch intermittently loses a packaged app's first window since 1.64.0
  • #43242 [Regression]: Chromium 155+ aborts a preflighted cross-origin redirect whenever any route is registered (net::ERR_ABORTED)

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

Changelog

Sourced from @​testing-library/react-native's changelog.

14.1.0

Features

  • Added fireEvent.layout() to simulate the layout engine measuring an element, invoking the onLayout handler with a synthetic layout event. Unlike fireEvent(element, 'layout'), it does not bubble to parent elements.
  • fireEvent.scroll() and userEvent.scrollTo() use the size from the last layout event on the same ScrollView as the default layoutMeasurement.
  • Added userEvent.accessibilityAction() to dispatch a named accessibility action to an element, invoking its onAccessibilityAction handler.
  • Added userEvent.pullToRefresh() to simulate the pull-to-refresh gesture on a host ScrollView element, invoking the onRefresh handler of its refreshControl prop.
  • Added the eventDiagnostics configuration option. When enabled, fireEvent and userEvent log a warning when no handler is called, e.g. because the target is disabled, blocked by pointerEvents, or has no handler for the event. Off by default. See the configuration docs.
  • Added support for React 19.3 (with test-renderer@1.3) and React Native 0.88.

Bug fixes

  • userEvent.scrollTo() emits a scroll event for the last step of a drag scroll, matching native behavior, and no longer emits scroll events when the scroll offset does not change.
  • Fixed the setImmediate fallback in environments without it (e.g. jsdom) picking up Jest fake timers, which could make async utilities hang.

Deprecations

  • fireEvent warns when a direct event bubbles from a nested element to the host element that emits it, e.g. scroll from ScrollView content to the ScrollView. These events will stop bubbling in the next major version. See the fireEvent docs for the list of direct events.

Release startup could change retained SQLite before inventory, maintenance activation accepted a PostgreSQL URL without proof of reconciliation, and recovery checks printed counts without asserting matching data.

Preparation now preserves and inventories SQLite/WAL and disk media before first startup without entering import maintenance. The existing protected release workflow supports prepare-only dispatch; normal qualified SQLite deployment with cutover false brings retained data to the current schema before bootstrap and the freshly quiesced import. Import receives the exact new manifest. PostgreSQL activation requires a matching environment/manifest receipt and fresh table-hash checks; resume cannot bypass import activation. SQLite abandonment and recovery-mode resume remain supported.

Logical backups fingerprint and dump the same exported read-only PostgreSQL snapshot, then assert restored table sets, counts and canonical hashes. Managed rehearsal stops writers, pins restore to the captured recovery baseline and checks restored and still-stopped data. Both provider waits share one 45-minute deadline measured after assuming the 60-minute identity, reserving cleanup time. Live retained-file writer discovery remains privileged and fails on inaccessible descriptors; fixtures use a controlled proc tree. Shell fixture paths are passed through an environment variable instead of interpolated into shell source.

Validation: test:fast; focused operation fixtures (7/7), including resume bypass and combined deadline exhaustion; nonroot Linux preservation/writer-permission fixture; normal commit/push hooks, including the full prepare → SQLite install/migration → bootstrap → drain → fresh manifest import sequence. PostgreSQL tests (12/12, no skips) and a real pg_dump/pg_restore under concurrent writes were also validated earlier in this PR. Scoped format/lint, shell syntax and diff checks pass.

Release cutover stays false. No AWS mutation, hosted rehearsal, deployment or merge was performed. Live retained-data inspection/recovery, manually launched worker shutdown, device/OTP and protected approvals remain operational gates. Unblocks the `main` promotion (#531), whose `Web export and browser checks` job failed on `chat-keyboard` and `video-file-fallback`. That job is skipped on `dev` PRs, so the failure went unnoticed.

The local/test web proxy (`scripts/production-web-proxy.mjs`, used by the browser smoke server, `run-real-local` and e2e; hosted uses nginx) had two realtime bugs:
- When the browser disconnected, the upstream request was never destroyed, so every closed page kept its SSE stream open against the runtime's 5-streams-per-account limit. All signed-in specs share one member, so later chat specs got a 429, shown as "Couldn't load the chat — The realtime chat connection was interrupted".
- The 5 s upstream request timeout also applied to open event streams, which only send a heartbeat every 15 s.

Fix: destroy the upstream request when the client response closes before finishing, and clear the timeout once the response is `text/event-stream`. A new test in `tests/web-deployment.test.mjs` fails without the fix and passes with it.

Before the fix, `chat-keyboard` failed 5 of 8 runs on a `dev` baseline. After it, the full Playwright suite passed 41/41 on three consecutive local runs.

This branch also merges `origin/main` (only the #421 merge commit, with no content change) so that `dev` contains `main` and #531 is no longer BEHIND.

body:
Refs #363, #364 (see also #169). Spec: `doc/planning/sprints/sprint-3-cognito/prompt.md`.

## What changed

- **Server** (`server/src/auth/cognito.ts`, `http.ts`, `config.ts`): authorization code + PKCE through Cognito Managed Login. `/api/auth/cognito/start` and `/api/auth/callback` check `state`, replay, ID token (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, `token_use`), `nonce` and `email_verified`, then issue the existing opaque Rewind session. New `cognito_sub` column (migration 031, SQLite and PostgreSQL). Session idle expiry is now 7 days. Sign-out returns the Cognito `logoutUrl`. Account deletion for Cognito accounts is a typed `DELETE` plus `AdminDeleteUser`, then the existing purge. `POST /auth/profile` saves the display name asked on first sign-in.
- **Password sign-in switch**: `REWIND_AUTH_PASSWORD` (default true: local, tests, hosted dev). `/auth/login` and `/auth/register` return 403 when false. `parseConfig` refuses to start when the media or database environment is `release` and it is true.
- **Client** (`App.tsx`, `src/auth`, `src/real/Settings.tsx`): "Continue with Cognito" is the main action, with a small "Developer sign-in" link to the existing form where password sign-in is on. Release shows only Cognito. First-sign-in name screen, `auth_error` notices, typed-DELETE deletion, Cognito sign-out. Native builds never show Cognito.
- **Terraform** (`infra/terraform/media/cognito.tf`): user pool (email + password, self sign-up, no MFA, Essentials), prefix domain, public app client with callbacks derived from `web_origins`, Warm Glass Managed Login branding. Runtime IAM user gets `cognito-idp:AdminDeleteUser` on that pool only. Hosted env gains `REWIND_AUTH_PASSWORD` and four `REWIND_COGNITO_*` keys (also added to `deploy/release-host.sh` and `deploy/compose.yaml`). The release module call sets `auth_password = false`.
- **Docs**: `AGENTS.md` product decision updated; design decisions and trade-offs in `doc/planning/sprints/sprint-3-cognito/design-decisions.md` (copied below).

## Design decisions

See the file for the full table. Highlights: public client + PKCE; Cognito accounts keep the NOT NULL password columns filled with random unusable values (no table rebuild); username `cognito-<hex>`, email not stored; display name asked on first sign-in; in-memory used-state set for replay; same-origin return paths only (carries the invite link through the redirect); redirect URI built from the request host, which Cognito validates against the exact callback list.

Trade-offs for speed: deletion protection off, default Cognito email sender, 10-character password minimum, one-day tokens, `/real/*` does not refuse an empty display name (the client gates it).

**IAM change you should review:** the Terraform apply role (`infra/terraform/bootstrap/access.tf`) gained `"cognito-idp:*"` because it could not create a user pool. Owner authorised this in the session. Applied to the bootstrap root.

body:
Refs #261, #172, #175. Follow-ups: #504 (release database), #505 (lossless rollback export).

## Why
The proposal names **PostgreSQL** as the relational store (§6) and requires backups by **the selected managed database backup mechanism** (§5.3). Hosted dev still ran on a SQLite file, so neither requirement was met.

## What
**PostgreSQL in the server, without rewriting persistence.** A worker thread owns a `pg` client and the caller blocks until each statement returns, so the ~300 synchronous `prepare/run/get/all/exec` call sites run unchanged. SQLite's semantics are kept on purpose:
- one serialised writer, with a 5 s busy timeout that ends in "database is locked";
- each statement in a transaction runs in a savepoint, so a failed statement does not abort the transaction;
- a `SAVEPOINT` outside a transaction opens one;
- error and row shapes match node:sqlite.

The SQLite idioms the code actually uses are translated at the boundary (`server/src/postgres/translate.ts`); anything that cannot be translated faithfully fails at `prepare`. `server/migrations/postgres/030-baseline.sql` reproduces SQLite migrations 1–30 and is checked column by column. The design is in `docs/architecture/ADR-0003-postgresql.md`.

**Data transfer from S3.**
- `deploy/database-import.sh` fetches a backup set from the backup bucket and validates it with the existing manifest checks.
- It then runs `cli.js database-import`: one transaction, deferred FKs, each value's type checked, and each table's row count and content hash reconciled before commit. Anything inexact commits nothing.

**Managed infrastructure** (`infra/terraform/media/database.tf`):
- Lightsail PostgreSQL 17: private, encrypted at rest, TLS verified against the RDS CA, daily snapshots with 7-day point-in-time restore.
- Terraform generates admin, `rewind_app` and `rewind_readonly` logins and delivers them through the existing hosted settings object; nobody handles them.
- A reviewed per-environment `enabled`/`cutover`/`bundle` switch; `cutover = false` is the rollback.

**Operations** (`Database operations` workflow, deploy role over temporary SSH): `status`, `bootstrap` (least-privilege roles), `import`, `resume`, `backup`, and `rehearse-restore`. The rehearsal restores to a new tagged database, verifies it, reports RPO and RTO, and deletes it. The nightly backup becomes a read-only `pg_dump`, verified by restoring it into a throwaway container before upload. The runbook is `docs/architecture/postgresql-operations.md`.

**Failover handling in the app:**
- dropped connections are replaced on the next statement;
- an in-flight transaction fails once and rolls back;
- `/health` fails while the database is unreachable and reports `checks.database`;
- each database is bound to one environment, and a runtime pointed at another environment's database refuses to start.

## Latency (owner request: fewer, cheaper database calls)
Measured per request with the new `Server-Timing` header (`scripts/measure-database-calls.mjs`, PostgreSQL):

| Request | Round trips before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST chat message | 38 | 6 |
| GET chat history | 15 | 5 |
| GET /archive | 21 | 2 |
| GET /contributions | 14 | 4 |
| GET /real/groups/current | 8 | 3 |
| GET /auth/session | 5 | 0 |

Two changes produce this:
- **One round trip per statement.** Each statement now travels with its lock or savepoint, with values as typed, escaped literals; the busy timeout becomes `lock_timeout`.
- **Cached signed-in identity**, as the owner directed. Session, selected group and membership are cached for 5 minutes, and the server's own sign-out, reset, deletion, group selection and invite acceptance clear them. The session's idle expiry is written at most every 10 minutes.

Chat sends also dropped the second membership check. A full async rewrite was not needed at this call count; the hosted measurement will confirm.

## Removed
- **The `/admin` table browser and its Terraform password** (owner request). Data is now browsed with any PostgreSQL client using `terraform output database_readonly_url`.
- **Dev database access.** Dev is publicly reachable for that purpose (`public = true`); TLS and the generated logins are still required.

## Tests
- **New Quality job, Server tests on PostgreSQL** (PostgreSQL 17): the whole server suite. Locally: 426 pass, 34 SQLite-internals tests skipped. On SQLite: 452 pass, with the 8 PostgreSQL-only tests skipped.
- **`server/tests/postgres.test.mjs`:**
  - translation;
  - config validation;
  - schema parity;
  - transaction semantics and busy timeout;
  - reconnect after a terminated backend;
  - environment binding;
  - the import, with sign-in, chat and identity continuity afterwards;
  - import refusal and rollback on a fractional integer or a dangling FK;
  - the role bootstrap: the read-only role cannot write.
- Race and fault-injection tests now use real second connections and dialect-aware triggers, so they also run on PostgreSQL.
- **Browser, local server on PostgreSQL:** created an account, created a group, sent chat messages and reloaded. The rows are in PostgreSQL, and the scheduler's 10-minute cycle rollover ran on it.
- Deploy fixtures pass, including a new configure case for the database keys (set, cut over, cleared). `terraform validate` passes for the media and release roots.

## Safe to merge before infrastructure
Until `infra/terraform/media` is applied, the hosted settings carry no database keys, `REWIND_DATABASE_URL` is empty, and the runtime stays on SQLite. The deploy is a no-op for data.

## After merge
1. Apply `infra/terraform/media` (dev). The plan adds the database, three generated passwords, the bootstrap object and the deploy-role operations policy; updates the hosted settings and the #492 backup IAM; and removes the admin password.
2. Set the repository variable `REWIND_DATABASE_BOOTSTRAP_URI`, then run Database operations `bootstrap`, then `import`.
3. Set `dev.cutover = true` in a small PR, apply, and deploy. Then run `status`, check the hosted app, and run `rehearse-restore`.
title: PostgreSQL persistence, S3 import, managed backups and recovery

`usermod -aG rewind ubuntu` and `snap install aws-cli --classic`. `backup.sh --local-only` now succeeds there (`rewind-20261006T104253Z.*`).

- Read-only by construction: only fixed `SELECT`s run, and table names must match `sqlite_master` and are quoted.
- Hides credential columns (hash, salt, token, secret, password, push destination, device key, and Demo `sessions.id`). Escapes all output, sets a strict CSP and `no-store`.
- Off when the password is unset. Refuses plain HTTP that did not come through the HTTPS edge (same check as the auth routes). The password must be at least 16 characters.
- Terraform (`infra/terraform/media`) generates the password into the hosted settings object. The deploy delivers it (allowlisted in `release-host.sh` and passed through in compose). Read it with `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/media output -raw admin_password`.

## Checks
- New `server/tests/admin.test.mjs`: disabled, HTTPS-only, 401 paths, secret hiding, HTML escaping, unknown table, POST.
- `npm run test:fast` green. Lint, typecheck, format and architecture checks green.
- nginx config passes `nginx -t` in `nginx:1.31.5-alpine`, and `/admin` returns 302 to `/api/admin/`.
- I confirmed hosted CloudFront forwards `Authorization` on GET requests to `/api/*`.

## After merge
Apply `infra/terraform/media` (dev) so the settings object gets the password, then re-run the dev deploy.

Refs #453, #470, #468

## What changed
Owner decision (6 Oct 2026): the synthetic Demo is removed entirely. The real-account app is unchanged.

- **Client**: no Try Demo entry point. Removed `src/demo`, the Demo session/profile providers, the Demo repository and runtime repositories, `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEMO_ACCESS`, the Demo camera mode, and the Demo-only screens and providers (old ChatScreen, CapsuleProvider, ContributionLedger, ReminderSettings, RuntimeStatusCard). Demo branches were stripped from shared capture and archive code.
- **Server**:
  - Removed Demo sessions (`server/src/session`), Demo group creation and invites, `advanceDemoCycle`, synthetic clip generation, and the seed fixture (`demo-fixture.json`, `seedDatabase`, `restoreFixture`, `listProfiles`).
  - Removed routes: `/sessions/*`, `/demo/*`, `/cycles/demo/advance`, `/groups`, `/groups/current`, `/groups/:id`, `/invites*`, `/cycles/current`, `/cycles/history`, `/messages/:id`, `/jobs`, `/profiles`.
  - Shared routes (`/contributions*`, `/clips`, `/films`, `/downloads`, `/archive`, premiere, realtime) now accept only a real-account credential. `openDatabase` no longer seeds data.
  - `preflight` checks schema readiness instead of the five-member fixture.
- **Infra/deploy**:
  - Removed `deploy/reset-with-backup.sh` and the Demo steps in `lifecycle-smoke.mjs`.
  - The runtime image no longer copies `server/fixtures`.
  - nginx 503 text now says "The runtime is unavailable."
  - Removed `make run-demo`. `make run` is now an alias for `make run-real`, because real sign-in needs HTTPS or localhost.
- **Tests**:
  - Demo-only suites are deleted.
  - Shared server tests use a test-only fixture group (`server/tests/helpers/fixture-group.mjs`) or real accounts (`helpers/real-http.mjs`).
  - Responsive and accessibility Playwright specs now sign up and create a real group over a local HTTPS smoke origin.
  - The "Demo reset-to-reveal" production e2e, its harness and `build-artifact` are removed. `test:slow` now runs `test:real-account-e2e` in its place.
  - `test:full-cycle` and `test:production-e2e` are removed.
- **A11y fixes** found by the retargeted Axe run: the dock gets `role="tablist"`, the dialog scrim gets a button role, and `Switch` gets `aria-checked`. There is no allowlist.
- **Docs**: AGENTS.md product decisions (Demo removed; tag `demo-frozen-20261004` marks the last Demo state), README, UX-CONTRACT, deploy and infra READMEs, and domain docs.

## Decisions
- **Hosted dev infra is kept as-is.** `infra/terraform/demo`, the `rewind-demo*` resource and instance names, `demo_instance_enabled`, the power scripts and the `AWS_DEMO_*`/`REWIND_DEMO_*` workflow variables belong to the live hosted **dev** host. Only the name says "demo". Renaming them would replace the host or break the deploy. No Terraform-planned attribute changed; `terraform fmt` and `validate` pass.
- **Schema is unchanged; no migration.** The Demo-era tables and columns (`sessions`, `invites`, `profiles.is_synthetic`) and any existing Demo rows in hosted dev stay. Nothing reads them now. Dropping them is a separate migration if wanted.
- **Audit actors**: `server/src/audit` still records an actor only for synthetic `demo-*` profiles (a privacy allowlist). Real-account events keep a null actor, as before.
- The test fixture keeps its historical `demo-*` IDs, so shared-logic assertions read the same.

## Removed rather than retargeted
- The `staged_sources` = 0 after-revocation assertion.
- `/downloads` dropped from the readable-for-own-group list in `cross-group-access`.
- `full-cycle-scenario.test.mjs` (Demo reset → join → reveal journey). Real scheduler and real-archive suites already cover the real lifecycle.
- Demo-only server suites: `session-audit`, `session-http-policy`, `invites`, plus the Demo cases in `runtime` and `cycles` (reset, reveal, advance, profiles, synthetic clip).

## Checks run
- `format:check`, `lint` (0 errors; 2 warnings that were already in `tests/native-build.test.mjs`), `architecture:check`, `typecheck`.
- `test:fast`: root 164/164, server 442/442, Jest 529/529.
- `test:a11y`: 6/6.
- Playwright responsive suite: 35/36 when run in parallel. `injected-recording.spec.ts:75` passes 4/4 when run alone (`--workers 1`) but flakes under parallel CPU load on the moving-frame check.
- `test:real-account-e2e` times out at 120 s. It times out the same way on unmodified `origin/dev`, so this PR didn't cause it.
- Codex review (GPT-6.1 Sol, medium) raised two P2 findings, both fixed: `make run` could not sign in, and the smoke server opened HTTP before HTTPS was ready. No other findings.
- `make run-real`: Welcome has no Try Demo. Local register, sign-in, group creation, Home, Chat and Archive all work, and every API call returned 200.

body:
Fixes from the iPhone walkthrough of the merged Warm Glass UI (#440). Relates to #413 and #430.

The walkthrough ran on the merged `dev` build with test accounts on a local server behind HTTPS. Two lanes:
- iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5, real Safari): 37 of 43 screens reached.
- Playwright WebKit iPhone emulation plus Chromium with a fake camera: 34 of 39 screens reached.

## Fixed

| What people saw | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every form was covered by "Turn your phone upright" while typing (sign-up, sign-in, new group, delete account, chat box) | The iOS keyboard shortens the window until an upright phone reads as landscape | The portrait guard asks the browser how the device is held (`screen.orientation`, or the legacy angle) before using the window's shape |
| The film showed no picture on iPhone | A photo (full range) plus a browser recording (variable frame rate on a µs timescale) made x264 write full-range H.264 at **level 6.2**, which iOS Safari will not play | Clips, photos and films convert to TV range and pin High@4.0; the film is constant 30 fps. A/B checked in Simulator Safari: the old film won't play, the new one plays |
| A moment the owner removed before compile still went into the film | Compile queries ignored `removed_at` | Filter added to the four compile queries |
| Signed-out screens could be panned sideways | Decorative glows wider than the screen; only `body` clipped them | `html`, `body` and `#root` clip |
| Long-pressing a chat message selected its text | Actions opened only on tap | A long press opens the actions too, and the bubble text isn't selectable |
| Back/close buttons were 40 pt and text links about 20 pt tall | react-native-web ignores `hitSlop` | Icon buttons 44 pt; web text links at least 44 pt tall |
| The reminder switch turned on in iPhone Safari where push can't arrive | — | After saving, the Add to Home Screen steps open |
| "Your session has ended" after a deliberate sign-out | In-flight requests got a 401 after logout and set the revoked notice | 401s during sign-out are ignored |
| Film segment freezing could stop half-way (review follow-up) | Inserts ran one at a time | Runs in a savepoint (nests in the account purge) |

## Tests

- New tests:
  - `portrait-guard`: keyboard case.
  - `film-compilation`:
    - a photo plus a variable-rate clip compiles to High, level ≤ 4.0, yuv420p, TV range, 30/1;
    - a removed moment is left out of the film.
- Checks run, all passing: `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `architecture:check`, `test:fast`, `test:a11y`, `test:slow`.

## Not in this PR

The rest of the walkthrough and audit findings are filed as issues: photo review legibility, film end-screen buttons, the camera preview on first open, the small-phone chat with the keyboard open, offline sign-in, and the audit's High findings.

body:
Rebuilds the real-account app in the Warm Glass design from the final screen set, and adds the server support those screens need. Relates to #413, #428, #429 and #430 (not closing them here).

The Demo stays frozen. It keeps working, and only its shared entry and capture surfaces changed. Reminders are web push only, and iOS ships as the PWA.

## What changed, by flow

- **Shell.** The header shows the group name, which opens the group menu (G1/G2). The avatar opens Settings as a pushed screen. The dock has Home / Chat / Archive glass tabs plus a separate shutter with the 5-segment allowance ring. Dock rules follow each Home state.
- **Launch and entry (A, B, C).**
  - Cream launch screen with the campfire icon.
  - Welcome, with Try Demo as its own bottom sheet.
  - Username-only sign-in.
  - Create account as username + password + confirm, then the "account is ready" banner.
  - Terms and Privacy line. No email, phone, code or reset anywhere.
- **No group, join, create (D).** Six-letter codes auto-format as `ABC-DEF` and show the server's own messages. Create group has a name, a prompt (presets or custom) and a 2–10 member stepper. "Copy invite link" is gone.
- **Home (H).**
  - Countdown, week, prompt card, allowance row (opens Your moments) and this week's moments as metadata only.
  - Status cards for developing, taking longer, premiere and failed moments.
  - After sealing: the allowance row rolls and a "Sealed" tip appears.
- **Capture (V, P).**
  - Full-screen dark viewfinder with the photo/video switch and the moments-and-seconds pill.
  - Record ring with auto-stop.
  - Review with a trim strip (0.5 s minimum; arrow keys on the web) and the four looks.
  - Upload with cancel, upload failed with retry, and Sealed.
  - Pre-permission says **Continue**; Camera off has Open Settings and Check again.
  - File fallback restyled. #401 and #329 behaviour unchanged.
- **Your moments (M).** One delete a week, then retake. A failed moment offers retry or delete without using the weekly delete.
- **Settings (S).**
  - Account card and group block. The owner can edit Prompt, Time zone and Invite; members see them read-only.
  - Members → person (Report, Block) → report sheet.
  - Switch group, Have an invite?, Create a group.
  - Reminder switch with the S10 pre-prompt (Continue only) and S11 on iPhone Safari; Snooze for 7 days.
  - Help, Privacy and Terms.
  - Sign out with confirmation, and Delete account (S19–S20).
- **Chat (T).**
  - Restyled timeline with day separators and an "N new messages" divider.
  - ✨ / Reply / Report actions on each message.
  - Reconnecting and offline pills, "Not sent · Retry", couldn't load, and the premiere banner.
  - Unread badge on the dock. Blocked people's messages are hidden.
- **Archive (R).** This cycle's step on top, then earlier films (Watch opens the full-screen film), Show older films, first-cycle and error states.
- **Film (F1, F3, F4).**
  - Full-screen film with segment bar, tap zones and pause; hidden moments are skipped.
  - End screen: Talk about it in Chat, Replay, Save film, Save your own moments.
  - Report a moment, and owner "Remove this moment".
- **Reminder (N1).** The weekly reminder only; a tap opens Home for the right group.
- **PWA.** New icons (including maskable and apple-touch), launch images, and the cream theme and status bar. The offline page matches.

## Server changes

- Migration `029-member-reports`: reports can target a member as well as a message or contribution. `POST` reports takes exactly one of `messageId`, `contributionId` or `memberId`. Success is `201 {reported:true}`; failures are `400 invalid_report` or `404`.
- The ready premiere and each `/archive` film list `segments: [{contributionId, startSeconds, durationSeconds, hidden, mine}]`. `hidden` covers blocked authors, reported moments and removed moments for this viewer.
- `POST /real/groups/:gid/contributions/:cid/remove` lets the owner remove a moment from a film for everyone. Responses: 200, 403 for non-owners, 404. It adds the columns `removed_at` and `removed_by_account_id`.
- Public `/privacy`, `/support` and `/terms`, served by nginx, the production web proxy and the local runner. The service worker passes them through.
- Focused server tests for each of these. The server suite is 470/470.

| S1 Settings | ![](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/pr-assets/warm-glass-ui/S1-before.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/pr-assets/warm-glass-ui/S1-after.png?raw=true) |

The old app had no Settings screen, so "before" S1 is the settings area of the old Home. The images live on the `pr-assets/warm-glass-ui` branch, which can be deleted after merge.

Walkthrough fixes are in this branch:

- Web dialogs sat under the dock; they now render through a portal.
- Pushed screens could be shifted sideways; the app root now clips overflow.
- The film did not autoplay reliably on the web; it now restarts once the source is ready, and the play button follows the player.

- Message bubbles were not announced as buttons; they now have the button role.
- The camera screen had lost its route heading; it is back as a hidden heading.
- Trim handles had no keyboard support on the web; arrow keys now move them.

Codex review fixes (see the review comment): frozen film segment timing that survives account deletion; Archive films play only through the filtered full-screen player; Home and Your moments count only the current week; Your moments has Try again after a failed load; a reported message leaves the open Chat; Chat keeps the reader's place when history loads; web dialogs make the page behind inert and manage focus.

## Known gaps and deviations

- **S19** copy follows the app: there is no email or phone, so nothing is sent.
- **R4** opens the full-screen film rather than playing in the card. The full-screen player renews playback access and skips hidden moments.
- **Dock unread badge** counts from app open (live stream only). A server-side read marker would make it survive reloads.
- **F3** has no cast button.
- **Removed or hidden moments** are skipped in the player, but they stay inside the already compiled MP4, so Save film includes them. Moment removal writes no audit entry.
- **Camera**: no photo upload cancel, no flash or flip control, and no "hold longer" rule.
- **Invite screen** keeps showing a code after someone uses it until it is reopened.
- **Under one day**, the Home countdown still says "1 day".
- **Safari locally**: WebKit won't keep the Secure session cookie on `http://localhost`, so signed-in Safari checks need the hosted HTTPS dev URL. The Reduce Motion pass ran in Chromium.

## Still needs the owner's iPhone

- #329, #348 and #401 capture checks in Safari and the installed PWA.
- Web push: S10 → permission → a Sunday reminder arrives, and tapping it opens the right group.
- PWA install: icon, launch image and cream status bar from the Home Screen.

body:
## Summary

Adds Vigolium native DAST and a bounded external-provider agentic trial for Rewind. Native scanning uses configured checks; the agentic trial uses OpenAI to plan probes and generate custom detectors against a disposable Rewind backend. No local AI model is required.

The agentic workflow validates fixture, chat, groups, and access-control/invitation scenarios. Authorized trial-branch and dev pushes run the offline gate followed by live trials; PRs targeting dev run offline checks without provider credentials. Redacted HTML reports and coverage summaries are retained for seven days.

## Linked issues

- No linked issue supplied for this setup trial.

## Run and review

- Base branch: `dev`
- How to see the change: review the successful [trial run](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/actions/runs/37184737791), download `vigolium-agentic-access`, and open `summary.html` for the scenario matrix or `report.html` for findings.
- Offline access verification: `node scripts/run-vigolium-rewind.mjs --verify --endpoint access` after building the scanner/backend images.
- Live trials require the repository `OPENAI_API_KEY` secret. They send synthetic HTTP traffic and disposable credentials to OpenAI; Rewind source and real user data are not supplied.
- Reviewer needed for sensitive change: yes, for security workflow, provider data handling, and scan isolation. This PR changes test tooling rather than application authentication behavior.

## Verification

- Commit `3d1dc6bd0e14334144a0ff8f7671cfca67dd88c4`: [GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/actions/runs/37184737791) passed.
- Applicable Quality checks: formatting, lint, typecheck, root tests, server/frontend tests and coverage, and cloud-free deployment fixtures passed. Browser checks were skipped under the existing main-only policy.
- Offline harness and container-isolation checks passed.
- Live fixture detected the intentional SQL injection and independently confirmed it against a parameterized control.
- Live chat and groups SQL injection trials passed; no vulnerability findings were reported.
- Live access trial made 49 scanner requests and exercised all 16 required owner/member/outsider/invite-recipient scenarios, with no failed or skipped scenarios and no vulnerability findings.
- Full local `npm run test:fast` failed on existing Windows/environment-sensitive checks; the Linux Quality run passed. Local focused harness tests, lint, and formatting passed.

## Known limitations

- Latest dev changes are included in the trial branch. The PR remains draft; no approval or merge has been performed.
- Coverage is scoped to chat/groups SQL injection and explicit access/invitation scenarios. Browser XSS, session revocation, uploads, and other endpoints remain untested by this trial.
- Detector generation is nondeterministic: an earlier fixture run needed one retry after generation failed. Incomplete generation or missing access scenarios fail the gate rather than reporting a clean scan.
- Generated detectors run as untrusted code in disposable workers. The target proxy restricts forwarded traffic; it is not a complete egress sandbox for agent tools.
- Successful scans are evidence of tested scenarios, not proof of whole-app security. Findings require review, and the first automatic dev run must be verified after an authorized merge.

## Latest fixes and validation

- Head `0c227f7`: fixed the proxy destination data flow and generated-artifact read race; disposable credentials now travel through captured stdout/stdin pipes, without a target.json credential file or backend Docker log storage.
- All nine CodeQL alerts are cleared by code changes, not dismissals. CodeQL and applicable Quality checks passed.
- The [latest branch trial](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/actions/runs/37277466740) passed offline isolation and all four live trials, including independent fixture detection and all required access scenarios.
- Provider planning now has bounded completion headroom (8-minute plan, 9-minute CLI, 10-minute container). Only transient fixture generation failures can retry once; failed detection verdicts and auth errors remain failures.
- Read-only review of the hardening and deadline changes found no actionable issues. This is not a PR approval.
- Remaining check: GitGuardian incident 37872283 flags a Username Password match in src/auth/real-account-client.ts's registration-validation helper, imported from dev. Inspection finds validation/error labels rather than a hardcoded credential at the reported location; the exact matched values require signed-in dashboard review before false-positive triage. No alert was dismissed and no authentication behavior changed to bypass the check.
title: Add native and agentic Vigolium DAST trials

body:
Server and config work for App Store submission (parent #427). The UI is being rewritten, so this PR adds no in-app screens or links.

Refs #428, #429, #430, #431, #432

## What changed

- **#428 Account deletion:** `POST /auth/account/delete` with `{ password }`. It needs a valid session and re-checks the password against the per-account login throttle (403 wrong password, 429 throttled). In one transaction:
  - A group the account owns passes to its longest-standing other member. A group with no other members is deleted with all its content.
  - The account's clips and photos are tombstoned (`status = 'deleted'`, paths cleared), then removed from disk or S3 after the commit.
  - Upload intents and invite-acceptance references, which do not cascade, are cleared.
  - The account row is deleted, which cascades to the profile, sessions, memberships, chat messages, reactions, reminders, reports and blocks.
  - Group films that were already compiled keep the deleted user's clips, because the films belong to the group. The privacy policy says this.
- **#429 Report and block:**
  - Migration 028 adds `content_reports` and `account_blocks`.
  - `POST /real/groups/:id/reports` takes `{ messageId | contributionId, reason? }`.
  - `GET` / `POST /real/blocks` takes `{ profileId }`, and `DELETE /real/blocks/:profileId` removes a block. A user can block only someone they share a group with.
  - Chat history and the SSE stream hide reported messages and blocked members' messages from that viewer only.
  - Operators list reports with `SELECT * FROM content_reports ORDER BY created_at`.
  - Not in this PR:
    - owner removal of other members' content
    - hiding a blocked member's clips inside an already-compiled film
- **#430:** public `privacy.html` and `support.html`, served from the web build. Support goes to GitHub Issues.
- **#431:** specific camera and microphone purpose strings, and `ios.infoPlist.ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false`.
- **#432:** no change needed. Native sign-in already stores the token in SecureStore and sends `Authorization: Bearer`, and `server/tests/real-account-auth.test.mjs` covers this.
- Tests that hardcode the latest migration version now expect 28.

## Checks that ran

- `server/tests/account-safety.test.mjs` (new) covers:
  - delete with the wrong password, with no session, and with success
  - after deletion: session revoked, login fails, ownership transferred, solo group removed, media file removed, the other member's chat intact, username reusable
  - report validation and hiding
  - block, list and unblock
- `npm run test:fast`: all green (145 + 468 + 632 tests).
- `lint`, `typecheck` and `architecture:check` pass.
- `make run-real` style local run (`real-local`), driven by curl through `/api`: register, create a group, delete with the wrong password (403), delete (200), then session check (401). Both static pages render in the browser.
title: App Store readiness: account deletion, report/block, privacy pages, iOS config

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072

4.37.5 - 03 Aug 2026

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

  • This version of the CodeQL Action adds support for the tools input for the codeql-action/init step to be specified using a github-codeql-tools repository property. This feature will gradually be rolled out following the release of this version. Once rolled out, this allows for the CodeQL CLI version that is used in GitHub-managed workflows, such as Default Setup, to be set to a custom value. For example, customers who run into issues with rate limits when a new CodeQL CLI version is released can set the value to toolcache to always use the CodeQL CLI version that is available in the runner toolcache. For Advanced Setup workflows, the value provided for tools in the workflow definition always takes precedence unless the value of the repository property starts with !. #4037

title: test(browser): accept VP9 video from open-source Chromium recordings

body:
Unblocks promotion PR #421. Its `main`-only browser checks failed 2/32: `injected-recording` expected AAC, but CI's Linux Chromium can't encode AAC and records MP4 with Opus. Safari (the iPhone PWA) and Chrome record AAC, and the server re-encodes either way. The decoded-tone assertions (RMS and zero crossings) still prove the audio is present and correct.

Checks: `injected-recording.spec.ts` passes 4/4 locally; `format:check` passes.
title: test(browser): accept Opus audio from open-source Chromium recordings

Promotes the accepted `dev` work to `main`: 382 commits since 27 Sep. Merging deploys `main` to the new **release** environment (#230) at https://d2r0xzy7vz590e.cloudfront.net through `.github/workflows/deploy-release.yml`.

**Needs one approving review from a collaborator other than the author** (`main` protection applies to admins too).

## Highlights since the last promotion
- Real-account app: bottom navigation, capture fixes, landscape capture, iPhone camera sheet for photos, 1080p in-page video, retro looks before upload (#407, #414, #415, #419)
- Hosted dev: private S3 media, scheduled web push reminders, settings delivered by Terraform with no manual secrets (#416, #417)
- Observability: request timing, client timing marks, host alarms (#418)
- Deploy reliability: release pruning and disk checks (#409); release environment (#420)
- Configurable cycle length and a 720p film (#411, #414)

## Checks
`dev`'s Quality and CodeQL are green on every merged PR. This PR also runs the `main`-only browser checks.

body:
Refs #230.

## Live now (applied with `rewind-terraform-apply`)
- **URL**: https://d2r0xzy7vz590e.cloudfront.net (serves once the first release deploy runs)
- **`infra/terraform/release`** (own state, `rewind/release/terraform.tfstate`): 21 resources added, nothing changed or destroyed.
  - **Host**: Lightsail `rewind-release` (micro, Ubuntu 24.04, same `cloud-init.sh`) with a static IP. Port 80 is open for the CloudFront origin; 22 only through Lightsail connect.
  - **HTTPS**: a CloudFront distribution with a Terraform-generated `X-Rewind-Origin-Auth` secret.
  - **Deploy role**: `rewind-release-deploy`, OIDC-trusted only for `environment:release` (by name and by immutable ID) on `refs/heads/main`, and limited to the release host.
  - **Media**: the `media` root reused as a module with `environment=release`, giving a separate bucket, IAM user and settings object. Through the new `extra_hosted_settings` variable that object also carries the web bind, the allowed origin and the origin secret.
- **GitHub**: a `release` environment that only `main` may deploy to, plus repository variables `AWS_RELEASE_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, `REWIND_RELEASE_INSTANCE` and `REWIND_RELEASE_HOSTED_ENV_URI`.

## In this PR
- **`.github/workflows/deploy-release.yml`**: Deploy dev's verified path (Quality gate, release bundle, health checks, automatic restore) for `main`. The human gate is `main`'s required review.
- **`release-host.sh configure`**: creates a private `rewind.env` on a brand-new host before the first install, so the release host never inherits the dev example (and its dev backup settings).
- **`media` root**: optional `extra_hosted_settings`. Dev plan: **No changes**.

## Checks run
- Terraform: validate and plan for release (21 to add), apply; dev media plan shows no changes; `fmt` passes.
- `tests/deploy/release-configure.test.sh` now covers a fresh host (file created with mode 600). All deploy fixtures and Terraform/root tests (92/92) pass.

## Not yet done
- The first release deploy needs this work on `main`. Promoting `dev` → `main` needs one approving review from a collaborator other than the author.
- The demo cost audit will list the release host as unexpected until its allowlist (demo root variables) is updated.

body:
Refs #366, #367

## What
- Four original retro looks replace the two server-only looks for new captures: **Disposable Flash**, **Compact Digital** (`ccd`, default, orange date stamp), **8mm Home Movie** and **VHS Camcorder**. The server still accepts `soft-focus` / `high-contrast` for existing rows and older clients.
- **Web applies the look on the device before upload**, for photos and videos:
  - Photo: drawn on a canvas (long edge capped at 2160 px), graded, exported as JPEG 0.9; those bytes are uploaded.
  - Video: the trimmed segment plays in a hidden `<video>`, each frame is drawn to a canvas, `canvas.captureStream(30)` plus the source audio through Web Audio (`createMediaElementSource` → `createMediaStreamDestination`, because Safari lacks `HTMLMediaElement.captureStream`) is recorded with the in-page MP4 recorder type at 8 Mbps, max 1080p. It uploads already trimmed (trim 0..duration). Shows "Applying retro look… N%" with Cancel; a failure shows a readable error and keeps the original for retry.
  - Drawing is in the pure `src/capture/retro-looks.ts`; the browser pipeline is `src/capture/retro-browser.ts`.
- **No double application**: uploads send a validated `clientProcessed: true`; the job stores `client:<look>` and the worker only normalizes (FFmpeg `null` filter). Uploads without the flag get FFmpeg approximations of the same four looks.

## Deviation (native, #367)
Native apps (and browsers that cannot re-encode MP4) upload the original. The **server applies the look** with FFmpeg after upload. So native retro runs server-side, not "before upload" as #367 asks. Real on-device native processing would need a new native media module and rebuilt binaries.

## Checks run
- `npm run test:fast`: node 144/144, server 464/464, jest 632/632
- `npm run test:responsive`: 32/32. The injected-recording spec now records a real clip, picks VHS, runs it through the browser retro pipeline (ffprobe/PCM check on the processed H.264/AAC bytes: tone preserved, ~3.5 s, 360×640) and uploads it with `clientProcessed: true` → 201.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint` (0 errors), `npm run typecheck`
- Local `make run-real`-equivalent: a real account photo upload with VHS, CCD and 8mm looks went through client grading → `clientProcessed` upload → sealed.
- New tests: `tests/retro-looks.test.ts`; server tests for all six modes processing with real FFmpeg, mode/flag validation, client-processed pass-through vs native look application (clip + photo), and the upload-intent path storing `client:vhs`.

Not verified: real iPhone Safari (gesture/audio unlock, `ctx.filter` fallback path) and hosted S3 direct transfer.
title: feat(capture): retro looks before upload (#366, #367)

## Problem

The first `Deploy dev` run after #324 merged failed at the OIDC step:
`sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` returned `AccessDenied`, so nothing was
installed on the host.

CloudTrail showed the subject GitHub actually presented:

```
repo:Collaboration95@68595032/rewind-app@1354608509:environment:dev
```

The repository issues **immutable** OIDC subject claims
(`GET /repos/Collaboration95/rewind-app/actions/oidc/customization/sub` ->
`use_immutable_subject: true`, prefix
`repo:Collaboration95@68595032/rewind-app@1354608509`). The trust policy
pinned only the classic `repo:Collaboration95/rewind-app:environment:dev`,
so no token could ever match.

## Change

* Pin both exact subjects, with no wildcard, so the environment-scoped role
  matches today's immutable tokens and still matches if immutability is
  toggled later.
* Fix the assume step's caller-identity self-check. It verified using
  credentials written to `$GITHUB_ENV`, which only reaches later steps, so it
  failed with `NoCredentials` once the assume began succeeding.

## Validation

* `terraform plan -target=aws_iam_role.deploy` showed exactly one in-place
  change: the `sub` condition gaining the immutable subject. Applied with the
  same target (IAM role only; no other resource touched).
* `terraform fmt -check`, `terraform validate`, and
  `tests/terraform/demo-deploy-policy.test.mjs` (9 tests) pass.
* CloudTrail confirms GitHub presents the immutable subject for this repo, so
  the new value is the one that matters.

## Note for reviewers

To unblock the merged deploy the trust policy was applied ahead of this
review, using `-target=aws_iam_role.deploy` so only that IAM role changed.
The running host, distributions, budgets, and the rest of the Demo root were
out of scope and untouched. A full un-targeted apply still shows pre-existing
drift (the live Demo root uses non-default variables such as enabled
distributions and budget recipients); that drift predates this change and is
not addressed here.
title: fix(ci): trust GitHub's immutable OIDC subject for the dev deploy role
